title: Reading climate change in your own home and community

say: Reading climate change in your own home and community.
This is the video for module one of Climate Awareness and Community Resilience.
People often say the weather has changed. What they usually mean is that the climate has changed.

panel.heading: What you will be able to do
items: Tell weather and climate apart
Explain the greenhouse effect in plain words
Collect local evidence of change
Find your household's top three vulnerabilities

say: Weather is what the sky is doing today or this week. Climate is the usual pattern over many years. The World Meteorological Organization uses 30-year averages, for example 1991 to 2020.

say: Sunlight passes through the air and warms the ground. The warm ground gives off heat back towards the sky.

panel.heading: The greenhouse effect in plain words
items: Sunlight warms the ground
The ground gives off heat
Greenhouse gases trap some heat
More gases, more trapped heat
Warmer air and sea

say: Some gases, called greenhouse gases, hold part of that heat in, like a thick wrapper on a sleeping baby.

panel.heading: The greenhouse effect in plain words
items: Sunlight warms the ground

More gases, more trapped heat
Warmer air and sea

say: But people have added much more of these gases, mainly by burning coal, oil and gas, and by cutting down forests. So more heat is held in, and the whole planet is warming.

say: That sounds small, but it is an average over the whole planet. A small rise brings many more very hot days and heavier downpours.

panel.rule: The UN reports the Earth is about 1.4°C warmer than the late 1800s.

say: Adaptation means changing how we live and work to reduce harm, like moving shop goods off the floor in the rainy season.

panel.heading: Three words for the whole course

cards.d: Changing how we live and work to reduce harm, like storing water before the dry season.
Reducing the gases we add, like using less charcoal or planting and protecting trees.
Absorbing a shock like a flood, recovering quickly, and coming back stronger, not poorer.

say: Mitigation means reducing the gases we add. For example, using less charcoal, or planting trees.

panel.heading: Three words for the whole course

cards.d: Changing how we live and work to reduce harm, like storing water before the dry season.

say: Resilience is the ability of a household to absorb a shock, recover quickly, and come back stronger rather than poorer.

say: Amina lives in a village near Bauchi. Her family notebook has the date of the first rain good enough for planting, every year.

panel.heading: Amina: is it weather or climate?
items: Her father wrote the first planting rain each year
2016 to 2020: average about 25 April
2021 to 2025: average about 15 May
About 20 days later on average
One late year is weather; a run of years is a pattern

say: She averages five years at a time. From 2016 to 2020, the planting rains came on average around 25 April. From 2021 to 2025, around 15 May.

panel.heading: Amina: is it weather or climate?
items: Her father wrote the first planting rain each year
2016 to 2020: average about 25 April
2021 to 2025: average about 15 May
About 20 days later on average
One late year is weather; a run of years is a pattern

say: So the rains now arrive about 20 days later on average.

panel.heading: Amina: is it weather or climate?
items: Her father wrote the first planting rain each year

2021 to 2025: average about 15 May
About 20 days later on average

say: One late year, like 2018, is weather. A whole run of later years is a sign of a shifting pattern.
Ten years is still shorter than 30, so she treats it as a strong warning sign and keeps recording.

say: Older residents can tell you what has changed on your street or farm. Invite three to six of them, including at least two women, and draw the twelve months.

panel.heading: Run a then-and-now seasonal calendar
items: Invite three to six elders, at least two women
Draw twelve months on paper or the ground
Then row: rains, heat, water and food shortages
Now row: the same questions for recent years
Count the shift in months

say: In the Then row, about 20 to 30 years ago, mark when the rains started and ended, the hottest time, and when water and food were hardest to get.

say: For example, in Esther's community in Benue, the rainy season went from about 6.5 months to about 5. That is about 1.5 months shorter.

say: Memory is strong for dramatic years. If only one person remembers a change, write it down, but mark it to check.

panel.rule: Trust a change more when several people agree and can name years.

say: Exposure asks whether the hazard reaches you at all. A shop on low ground is exposed to flooding.

panel.heading: Three parts of vulnerability
items: Exposure: does the hazard reach you?
Sensitivity: how badly does it hurt?
Capacity gap: how little you can fall back on
Score each from 1 to 3, total 3 to 9

say: Sensitivity asks how badly it hurts. A family that depends only on a rain-fed maize farm is very sensitive to late rains.

panel.heading: Three parts of vulnerability
items: Exposure: does the hazard reach you?
Sensitivity: how badly does it hurt?
Capacity gap: how little you can fall back on
Score each from 1 to 3, total 3 to 9

say: Capacity is what helps you cope: savings, stored water, a strong group, skills and good health.

panel.heading: Three parts of vulnerability
items: Exposure: does the hazard reach you?
Sensitivity: how badly does it hurt?
Capacity gap: how little you can fall back on
Score each from 1 to 3, total 3 to 9

say: Score water, food, income, health and housing from 1 to 3 on each part. Add them. The higher the total, the more vulnerable that area is.

items: Exposure: does the hazard reach you?

say: Ngozi sells provisions in Onitsha. Her shop scored 9, because her goods sit on the floor beside a drain that overflows. Heat for her elderly mother scored 8, and food prices 7.

panel.heading: Ngozi scores her household
items: Income 9: shop stock beside a drain that floods
Health 8: hot nights for her mother, aged 70
Food 7: all food is bought
Quick win: raise stock off the floor
Clear the drain and start a small saving

say: Cheap actions lower a score fast. She will raise her goods on pallets or blocks before the rains, clear the drain with her neighbours, and save a little each week in her ajo group.

say: An honest score of 9 that leads to action protects your family more than a hopeful 5 that hides the problem.

panel.rule: Score what is true today, not what you plan to do.

say: To remember. Climate is the long average, not one bad day. Extra greenhouse gases from human activity are warming the planet. Your family records and your elders are real evidence. And act first where your score is highest.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Climate is the long average, not one bad day
Extra greenhouse gases are warming the planet
Elders and family records are real evidence
Exposure, sensitivity and capacity make vulnerability
Act first on your highest score
